body:
My story starts on the front lines – not in politics.
| | |
---
| | [](https://xbdizvxp.r.us-east-1.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Freeves-for-senate%2Fforged-on-front-lines%3Futm_campaign=20251114_Reeves_ForgedOnFrontlines%26utm_id=CE%26utm_medium=email%26utm_source=ac/1/0100019aa3b7d5c4-c33e539b-fbd0-402f-a30d-a400de6b1e47-000000/HPXAAvXQgld8N32b904ULoGRdnY=453)
---
| |
---
| Peter, long before I ever ran for public office, I learned what service truly means. **I didn 't learn it from politics – I learned it from a life on the front lines.** In the Army, you learn quickly that leadership isn't something you claim. It's something you prove – _**through discipline, sacrifice, and the responsibility to protect the people standing beside you.**_ In law enforcement, you see the courage of the men and women who put their lives on the line every day for their communities – **_and you understand what real accountability looks like._** Those experiences shaped me far more than anything in Richmond or Washington ever could. **And they 're the reason I'm running for the United States Senate.**
---
| | [SUPPORT REEVES](https://xbdizvxp.r.us-east-1.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Freeves-for-senate%2Fforged-on-front-lines%3Futm_campaign=20251114_Reeves_ForgedOnFrontlines%26utm_id=CE%26utm_medium=email%26utm_source=ac/2/0100019aa3b7d5c4-c33e539b-fbd0-402f-a30d-a400de6b1e47-000000/_aUU3-2G38e6ACKNnW624pPqLnM=453)
---
| Because right now, our country is being held back by politicians who have never been tested – who talk endlessly about leadership but rarely demonstrate it. Mark Warner has spent decades in Washington mastering the art of political survival. But Virginians deserve something better: **_a Senator who knows what it means to serve, to protect, and to put others first._** That's the standard I live by. And it's the standard I'll bring to the Senate every single day.
---

name: The Blue Dogs
subject: Democrats with a backbone
body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119679789/583873671/1219929396?refcode=-header-&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk4MjcyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjA4ZmJiZmEyLTZkYzYtZjAxMS04MTk2LTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Z_y4kCQqrMcFGMCI7hB72jLHB_NDtmhxmROn3Z8l9Vw=) | Hi Peter, In Washington, there are plenty of people who know how to spend money. There are far fewer who are willing to ask the hard question: **How do we pay for it?** Blue Dog Democrats have never been afraid to be the adults in the room. They are the ones pressing both parties to cut waste, protect Social Security and Medicare, and make sure new ideas come with real plans, not just talking points. They know that if the numbers do not work on paper, the policy will not work in real life. You would think that kind of honesty would be rewarded. But instead, special interests and the extremes on both sides are lining up against them. They think fiscal responsibility is a slogan, not a standard. They want rubber stamps, not independent voices. **Blue Dog PAC exists to keep common sense in the room. We recruit, train, and support candidates who are willing to read every line of a bill, do the math, and tell the truth about what we can and cannot afford. #

President Trump is calling for me to be hanged.
I put out a video, alongside veterans of the military and former members of the intelligence community. It had a simple message: If you are serving in the military, you have an obligation to refuse illegal orders.
Trump’s friends in the White House didn’t like that. They accused us of insurrection.
At some point, the President heard about it, and he hasn’t stopped posting and reposting about us since — accusing us of sedition, calling for our arrest, calling for us to be hanged.
It is no small thing for the President of the United States to call for your execution. Elon Musk called me a traitor. Trump’s advisor, Roger Stone, called for me to be executed. And now Trump himself has called for me to be hanged.
As someone whose family has faced political violence before, I know you have to take words like this seriously, and that’s why I’m writing to you.
There’s no telling what kind of storm we’re heading into right now. Unfortunately, we need to be prepared for any outcome.

name: Barack Obama
subject: The other side isn’t finished with this nonsense
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President
body:
The work to decide who holds power in this country is happening right now.

---
Peter, The midterm elections may be a year away, but the work to decide who will win the House of Representatives is happening _right now_. Republicans know their policies aren’t helping people. The polls show that their agenda, and their leaders, are deeply unpopular. And in this month’s elections in New Jersey, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, we saw an electorate that is eager for a different path forward. That’s why Republicans have launched an unprecedented attempt to entrench themselves in power. In several Republican-led states, they’ve gerrymandered the maps so that they can avoid being accountable to the will of the people. Now, thanks to your support and the work of the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, they’re running into some real resistance. In California, voters overwhelmingly supported a temporary measure to counter the gerrymandering crisis. Other states are exploring following California’s lead. And in states like Missouri and Kansas, citizens are organizing to stop their leaders from using manipulated maps. Like many of us, voters overwhelmingly believe that the maps should be fair — because _elections_ should be fair. **But the other side isn’t finished with their assault on our democracy.** They are banking on other states, like Florida, Indiana, and New Hampshire, to enter the fray and continue the cycle of perpetual gerrymandering. And they’re asking the Supreme Court to strike down a critical part of the Voting Rights Act so they can throw out maps where communities of color have fair representation. **Attorney General Holder and I started the NDRC to safeguard democracy in moments like this.[That work has never been more important — which is why I’m asking for your support right now to help ensure we can keep up the fight against Republican power grabs.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119680184/583881011/-139457290?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_ObamaNov_email_20251120-NDRC-Tier1-ObamaNov_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20251120-NDRC-Tier1-ObamaNov_&utm_campaign=ObamaNov&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjY5MGQxMTFiLTZmYzYtZjAxMS04MTk2LTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=u1WH57q6GRgimb5Hg-a5ZGansEV_392RcADkl8nXCm0=)** | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

Peter, The midterm elections may be a year away, but the work to decide who will win the House of Representatives is happening right now. Republicans know their policies aren’t helping people. And in this month’s elections in New Jersey, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, we saw an electorate that is eager for a different path forward. That’s why Republicans have launched an unprecedented attempt to entrench themselves in power. In several Republican-led states, they’ve gerrymandered the maps so that they can avoid being accountable to the will of the people. Now, thanks to your support and the work of the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, they’re running into some real resistance. In California, voters overwhelmingly supported a temporary measure to counter the gerrymandering crisis. Other states are exploring following California’s lead. And in states like Missouri and Kansas, citizens are organizing to stop their leaders from using manipulated maps. Let me tell you more about The Atlas Society and how they are fundamentally changing the direction of our country.

_I will also tell you HOW The Atlas Society is spreading its message in what I consider one of the most innovative methods I 've EVER seen a nonprofit organization engage in before._

_**_So keep reading_!**_

My mentor, Andrew Breitbart, reminds us that politics is downstream from culture. But what is culture downstream from? Answer: Philosophy. That's where The Atlas Society shines, engaging young people with the virtues of reason, achievement, and benevolent self-interest in wildly creative, artistic ways.

Have you ever read Ayn Rand's _Atlas Shrugged_ or _The Fountainhead_?

These books changed how I saw the world and my role in it.

But they are 700+ pages long!

**Jennifer shared this terrifying statistic with me:** Daily reading of books among young people has fallen from 70% in the late 1970s to 12% today.

So, how do we preserve Rand's role as the greatest all-time recruiter for liberty? That's where The Atlas Society gets creative! They leverage art and technology to create programming for "_skimmers, swimmers, and deep divers_."

---
**Skimmers:** Social media memes and animated videos -- every single one of their 50 posts a week gets 40K comments, shares, and likes. The "Draw My Life" videos on concepts like Capitalism, Property Rights, and Free Speech reach MILLIONS of viewers. Links invite young people on a journey for deeper intellectual exploration.

**Swimmers:** Graphic novel adaptations of Ayn Rand's shorter books, Pocket Guides that distill big concepts like Postmodernism and Socialism into a 90-minute read. Weekly podcasts with top entrepreneurs and thought-leaders, and discussion groups like "Morals & Markets."

**Deep Divers:** They recruited an all-star academic faculty of philosophers and economists who guide students on a deeper study of Rand's philosophy, publish independent work, and provide programming at their summer conference for students (the Galt's Gulch Summit, where I spoke!).

name: Leaders We Deserve
subject: This isn’t about age, Peter
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
We’re building an intergenerational movement to power the leadership our democracy needs.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20251120-1&t=1&akid=2857%2E587540%2EbKUXWT)
Hi Peter. Let’s clear up a common misconception about Leaders We Deserve:
**Our mission is not “young people vs. old people.” It’s about fighters vs. folders — and that cuts across every generation.**
We focus so much on opening the door for young leaders because it’s been bolted shut for decades. This isn’t a new phenomenon. Wealthy donor networks, corporate PACs, and party machines have designed a system that makes it nearly impossible for younger candidates — and working-class people of _any age_ — to run for office and win.
At the end of the day, this work isn’t about age. It’s about electing leaders who will _actually fight for us_ — not ones who fold the moment their donors get uncomfortable or drag their feet while our planet burns.
And here’s the truth: we should never discount older generations, because real change only happens when all of us stand together, regardless of our age.
Leaders We Deserve would not exist without older Americans who want to see the status quo change and are fed up with watching the rights they spent their youth fighting for be ripped away. Many of our strongest grassroots supporters remember being young and feeling unseen by power, so now they’re determined to help pass the torch to a new generation of leaders. (Side note — not only did they fight for their generation, they literally opened the door for the next by lowering the voting age to 18!) We should all be extremely grateful for their support.
It’s far from just financial support that they bring, though. We rely on older people as mentors and examples. They marched for civil rights, protested wars, fought for reproductive rights, and defended democracy long before many of us were even born — laying the groundwork for our generation to lead youth-led movements on gun violence, climate action, racial justice, and more. We may be different ages, but we share a common belief: too many people in power simply are out of touch with our daily lives and struggles.
That’s why we built LWD: to finally open the door for community-rooted leaders of all ages who reflect our lived experiences. But it only works when we do it _together._
Look at Akbar Ali. He’s on the brink of becoming the youngest legislator in Georgia state history if he wins his runoff, made possible because Rep. Shelly Hutchinson, a longtime community leader, chose to step aside and lift up the next generation. That’s the model.
We see it in Speaker Pelosi passing leadership to the next generation. We see it at the No Kings protests, led in large part by older Americans. Some of them literally fought fascism and are showing up _again_ to defend our democracy, while I’m sorry to say, too many Gen-Z and millennials stay at home. If we feel fed up and pissed off by the status quo in our 20s and 30s, imagine how frustrated the generations before us feel. And yet, they still show up in overwhelming numbers every day to fight for a better future, _our_ future. Leaders We Deserve is here to empower young people to have a voice in power and to encourage older generations to pass the torch so new leaders can learn from them and be as effective as possible.
**That is what an intergenerational coalition looks like. And we need more of it.**
We endorse young candidates not _because_ they’re young, but because they’re the long-term investment our country desperately needs. And we need your help to keep building this bench.
**[Will you chip in today to help grow our movement and elect the next generation of leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251120_1_age.n0mN2G&refcode=em20251120-2857&amount=5&t=3&akid=2857%2E587540%2EbKUXWT)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251120_1_age.n0mN2G&amount=5&refcode=em20251120-2857&t=22&akid=2857%2E587540%2EbKUXWT)**
Thank you for helping build a future worthy of every generation, present and future.
— Leaders We Deserve

body:
#2 worst in America for insurance rate increases. Plus, New Mexico Ranked #1 Most Dangerous in America | New for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
**This is devastating.** New Mexico just got ranked #2 in the entire nation for the worst health insurance rate increases. [Some families are seeing 50% jumps](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=80ad87719b&e=567664f14c). | |
**INSURANCE RATES EXPLODING ACROSS NEW MEXICO**
Healthcare premiums are skyrocketing with increases that will crush family budgets:
United Healthcare wants a 52% increase. Blue Cross Blue Shield is pushing 40%. Presbyterian wants 30%. The average across the state is 35%.
Only Arkansas has it worse than us.
Mark breaks down who's really to blame here (hint: it's not just one party), and why this might be the rare moment where Democrats and Republicans actually come together to fight the insurance companies.
We dive into why Trump's team might jump on this issue and what it would mean for families getting crushed right now.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=16661f7e24&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
**NM RANKED #1 MOST DANGEROUS FOR SOLO TRAVELERS**
A new study gave New Mexico a safety score of 0 out of 100 — dead last in the nation for solo travelers. Our crime policies aren't just hurting families, they're now destroying one of our top industries: tourism.
**Mark connects the dots on how bad policy bleeds into everything — from healthcare costs to crime to economic development. When you don't put criminals behind bars, everyone pays the price.

****KELLER'S "POLICE KILLERS" AD BACKFIRES**
Tim Keller's new campaign ad claims Darren White's APD led to "shootings of innocent people." The Fraternal Order of Police is furious and demanding an apology.
Mark's take: "That language is ridiculous. It absolutely does not support cops whatsoever."
We break down the mayor's race, Darren's response, and why this matters for the December 9th runoff election.

name: Sarah McBride
subject: Congress finally voted to release the Epstein files
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Accountability and justice start now.
#
Hi — Sarah here with some important news.
**This week the House voted to release the full Epstein files.**
I voted yes because Epstein’s victims — and the American people — deserve truth, transparency, and justice. Anyone involved _must_ be held accountable, and we must make clear that no one is above the law, not even those with wealth, connections, or power.
If you’re confused by the whiplash from House Republicans, you’re not alone. After months of loudly demanding the release of the files, they suddenly reversed course once they learned Donald Trump’s name appeared in them.
Then just as suddenly, despite going to extreme lengths like blocking a duly elected Congresswoman from representing her constituents for 40+ days just to avoid the final signature on a vote, they changed their minds again.
**Still, no matter how we got here, this vote is a win for transparency, accountability, and justice for victims.**
I’ve been pushing for these files to be released since day one because every survivor deserves justice, and the American people deserve a government that doesn’t protect the powerful and well-connected. But this fight is far from over.
Given past efforts to limit or delay disclosure to protect Trump, there is real concern about political interference.
Because remember: Trump had the power this entire time to release these files _without_ an act of Congress. He’s only doing it now because the headlines were getting worse.
So, we cannot slow down. We need to demand full transparency _now_.
[**Will you add your name to call on the Department of Justice to release the full Epstein Files without delay? Survivors deserve nothing less.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/signup/em-20251120-epstein-files/?source=em20251120-2518&t=1&akid=2518%2E21716%2EemTun0)

clean_body: Accountability and justice start now. Hi — Sarah here with some important news. This week the House voted to release the full Epstein files. I voted yes because Epstein’s victims — and the American people — deserve truth, transparency, and justice. Anyone involved must be held accountable, and we must make clear that no one is above the law, not even those with wealth, connections, or power. If you’re confused by the whiplash from House Republicans, you’re not alone. After months of loudly demanding the release of the files, they suddenly reversed course once they learned Donald Trump’s name appeared in them. Then just as suddenly, despite going to extreme lengths like blocking a duly elected Congresswoman from representing her constituents for 40+ days just to avoid the final signature on a vote, they changed their minds again. Still, no matter how we got here, this vote is a win for transparency, accountability, and justice for victims. I’ve been pushing for these files to be released since day one because every survivor deserves justice, and the American people deserve a government that doesn’t protect the powerful and well-connected. But this fight is far from over. Given past efforts to limit or delay disclosure to protect Trump, there is real concern about political interference. Because remember: Trump had the power this entire time to release these files without an act of Congress. He’s only doing it now because the headlines were getting worse. So, we cannot slow down. We need to demand full transparency now. Thank you for taking a stand. — Sarah McBride

Hi there,

I wanted to take a moment to share something that makes me incredibly proud -- not just as a school board member, but as a lifelong resident of California’s Central Valley.

This week, Visalia Unified announced its graduation rate has climbed to an incredible 92% -- a milestone years in the making.

That number represents more than just statistics. It shows what’s possible when we invest in our students, empower our educators, and build community partnerships.

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rvfc-em-q4-2025?refcode=em-11.20.25-all-a [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rvfc-em-q4-2025?refcode=em-11.20.25-all-a] Visalia Unified Hits 92% Graduation Rate “These numbers represent more than progress. They represent partnership. Learning doesn’t happen in isolation. It thrives when students are empowered, families are engaged, and communities are connected,” -Superintendent Kirk Shrum

These achievements didn’t happen by accident -- they reflect years of work, advocacy, and investment from our school board and community. Here are just a few highlights:

* Over 13,500 students supported with extended learning programs
* Over 300 students placed in internships
* Significant upgrades to classroom technology and learning environments

As a member of the Visalia Unified School Board, I’ve been proud to champion investments in afterschool programs, classroom modernization, and stronger community partnerships that help students succeed both in and beyond the classroom.

But I’m not stopping there.

I’m running for Congress to continue fighting for public education -- for federal funding that truly reflects the needs of our students, and for working families who deserve more than what they’ve been given by politicians who’ve sold out to special interests.

Thank you for believing in this work and this movement.

In solidarity,

Randy Villegas

I'm running to represent NY-12 in Congress! This is the district where I was born and raised, and the place that five generations of my family have called home.

Hi friend, I'm Jack Schlossberg, and my grandfather, President Kennedy, is my hero.

In high school, I spent hours watching his speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. And that's exactly why I'm running for Congress.

[**This isn't going to be your average campaign — we’re at the forefront of a movement backed by real people who are ready for a new generation of leadership. I won't be bought or intimidated. Instead, I'll be relying on folks like you. So, if you're willing to be one of the first donors to my campaign, will you split a donation between myself and the Voter Protection Project right now? »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/96718?t=7&akid=21919%2E878179%2EErwUf8) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Jack Schlossberg and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/96719?t=8&akid=21919%2E878179%2EErwUf8)

I've always been passionate about politics — you can probably gather as much if you've seen any of my social media posts :) I pride myself on my hot (correct!) takes. But public service has always been my driving force. I come from a long legacy of public service, from my great-great-grandparents to my mother, Caroline Kennedy.

**I have big shoes to fill. I've known it all my life.** But this is even bigger than living up to my family name. This is about serving the people of New York — the city that shaped me into the person I am today.

Right now, our country is in crisis. Donald Trump and his buddies (my cousin RFK Jr. — to name just one) are tanking the economy, attacking free speech, and sowing distrust in decades of scientific research.

We need to revive empathy and effort. I want to be excited and feel hopeful about our future, and I want my fellow New Yorkers to feel the same way. I believe in a politics that works for the people it was intended to serve, and I'm ready to fight for it.

**And friend, I happen to think caring is cool.**

None of this will be easy. But in the words of my grandfather, I'm doing this "Not because it is easy but because it is hard."

Last night, Donald Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which was passed nearly unanimously by both chambers of Congress this week (only one House Republican member voted against it).
This kind of clear, bipartisan action is exceedingly rare in today’s politics. But when it came to pushing for accountability for Jeffrey Epstein and transparency for his survivors, Congressional Republicans ultimately joined Democrats and got it right.
Now do healthcare.
I mean, seriously — Republicans in Congress ought to step up and do their constitutional duty on more than just Epstein. Congress is a co-equal branch of our federal government, along with the President and the judiciary, and yet Republicans have been relinquishing that power and letting Trump run roughshod over congressional authority since the moment he took office.
It’s why so many of my 46 lawsuits against Trump (yes, 46 lawsuits in 43 weeks — the guy breaks the law a lot) center on how he’s overstepping his authority, and it’s why these lawsuits are necessary to restore that balance of power. Because Congressional Republicans don’t have the backbone to stand up to Trump most of the time.
This week we saw what can happen when public pressure pushes Republicans in Congress to defy Trump and join Democrats in working on behalf of the American people.
That kind of action was clearly necessary in this case — Epstein’s survivors deserved nothing less than a unified front from our leaders. But it shouldn’t be exclusive to cases of egregious, horrific criminality.
Californians and Americans deserve the same meaningful action when it comes to their healthcare. Their right to vote. Their reproductive freedom. Their children’s education.
If you agree, sign my petition today demanding Republicans in Congress do their jobs. We’ve seen that they’re capable — now they need a push to keep it going. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/pJ3P8XqgjE2vX8hD3lzNZQ2]

—Rob

Friends,
The Ninth Circuit has made a move in Zahid's case. They've handed his Emergency Motion for Release Pending Decision over to the district court (though they've kept jurisdiction over everything else) - and asked the court to process this emergency motion as a "habeas" petition for release from wrongful detention.
**This is good news.**
The federal district court at the Western District of Washington has a strong track record of backing immigrants, and is intimately familiar with the abuses and medical neglect present at the detention center. It is also the court best positioned to ascertain facts-on-the-ground and absolutely possesses the authority to compel ICE to release him.
As an emergency case - particularly one that was passed _down_ to them from the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, one level below the Supreme Court - this will catch their notice immediately. Due to the urgency of the situation it may well merit weekend action.
All this to say... _there 's a chance my beloved husband will be home for Thanksgiving._
I am grappling with a sense of disbelief in hope. It has been difficult to let myself feel joy, encouragement, or optimism, as I've processed this week's events - but I have found my way back to those emotions, thank goodness. The glimmers of reawakening of the possibility of sanctuary, solace, soul-joy with my spouse... it's hard to describe the beauty of the return of those feelings, or at least faith in their possibility.
* * *
I went in to see Zahid last night, with Salma. Just me and her, this time.
Zahid was in a tough place. The movie that had just been playing in the common room was an Indian film, full of violence, telling the story of a wrongfully detained man who seeks revenge on those who put him in there.
_**Side note** : what kind of psychological torture is it to play a film like that to a captive audience of wrongfully imprisoned men? And what kind of sadistic political sport, to imbue these men's psyches with this messaging... if any of them **are** released, and go on to commit crimes of revenge, just look at how they'll spin that up to validate the narrative of "oh look, criminal illegals, see, this is what we were saving you from! All the people we locked up are for your own protection!" Sheer abusive manipulation. Gaslighting, but with lives. _
Fortunately, Zahid's tough place evaporated into the sweetest imaginable beaming, gentle smile as he listened to his daughter's voice. Salma's conversation has developed in leaps and bounds, and she had stories she wanted to tell him, and she wanted to sing him the ABC song - in fact, right there over the phones and behind the glass, singing to her baba, was the first time I've ever heard her complete the full alphabet.
Then she laid on her back on the little metal counter, her head on the pillow of her sweater, and kicked her feet together to show him how the little lights flash and sparkle. He was smitten. Melted. Restored to peace. Soul healed, by her gentle innocence.
**This is what they 're depriving those fathers of. **
Brothers, husbands, sons. Friends, cousins, neighbors, coworkers. Teachers, employees, leaders, friends. Fathers.
The cruelty is breathtaking, and the callousness beggars belief.
Gratitude to everyone who fights this fight, who advocates, who goes and visits the ones who have no one, who keeps up the pressure. We need you. They need you. We can't do this without you. They can't do this alone.
Now that Zahid's case is before the district court, structured as an emergency habeas petition, things are likely to move fast. The court will probably docket the case by tomorrow morning (Friday). The judge will probably issue some form of ruling within 24-48 hours. They might seek more information, or they might immediately order his release - the timeline is impossible to predict exactly, but I put it at 70% odds he'll be home with us sometime in the next two weeks.
So I shift my attention to reintegration planning. Dim rooms, soft lights, healthy food, gentle touch, good work to do. _Medical care._ Reminders of home, familiar smells and flavors, time for whatever comes - bursts of chatter, hypervigilance, disrupted sleep, need for silence, emotional dysregulation, reduced mental processing capability... the combination of traumatic brain injury and chronic pain with months of unrelieved threat, overstimulation, sleep deprivation, nutritional insufficiency, and assaults on dignity, meaning, and hope - is not a gentle recipe.
He is an unusual person, truly remarkable in his gentleness, patience, flexibility, and good humor - but he is human, and he has been through one version of hell.
The fundraiser is still live - friends who would ask what you can do, that is one thing. Money stabilizes when all else is uncertain, and sustains the ability to be fully present and devote all my attention to co-regulation, to calm presence, to breathing and being beside him while he puts back together his soul.
[GoFundMe](https://substack.com/redirect/843cf464-91a5-4b88-a658-ddb70ae6d4f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meantime, friends, hug your families close please. Take a long walk on a beautiful autumn day and watch the leaves fall. Enjoy a good meal. Put down the phones. Do something kind for a neighbor; and do something to bring justice for someone more vulnerable than you. Remember that we weave the world together by our thoughts, our actions, our relationships. Remember that putting good out into the world is the purpose of our lives.
In the Quran, it says, that after a period of hardship, Allah grants ease. I will be grateful for the rest of my life for the love and support you have given. Our family is blessed, and I am committed to using what we've been given to help others.
The fight is not over. But we'll get through this - together.

They've handed his Emergency Motion for Release Pending Decision over to the district court (though they've kept jurisdiction over everything else) - and asked the court to process this emergency motion as a "habeas" petition for release from wrongful detention. This is good news. The federal district court at the Western District of Washington has a strong track record of backing immigrants, and is intimately familiar with the abuses and medical neglect present at the detention center. It is also the court best positioned to ascertain facts-on-the-ground and absolutely possesses the authority to compel ICE to release him. As an emergency case - particularly one that was passed down to them from the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, one level below the Supreme Court - this will catch their notice immediately. Due to the urgency of the situation it may well merit weekend action. All this to say... there 's a chance my beloved husband will be home for Thanksgiving. I am grappling with a sense of disbelief in hope. It has been difficult to let myself feel joy, encouragement, or optimism, as I've processed this week's events - but I have found my way back to those emotions, thank goodness. The glimmers of reawakening of the possibility of sanctuary, solace, soul-joy with my spouse... it's hard to describe the beauty of the return of those feelings, or at least faith in their possibility. I went in to see Zahid last night, with Salma. Just me and her, this time. Zahid was in a tough place. The movie that had just been playing in the common room was an Indian film, full of violence, telling the story of a wrongfully detained man who seeks revenge on those who put him in there. Side note : what kind of psychological torture is it to play a film like that to a captive audience of wrongfully imprisoned men? And what kind of sadistic political sport, to imbue these men's psyches with this messaging... if any of them are released, and go on to commit crimes of revenge, just look at how they'll spin that up to validate the narrative of "oh look, criminal illegals, see, this is what we were saving you from! All the people we locked up are for your own protection!" Sheer abusive manipulation. Gaslighting, but with lives. Fortunately, Zahid's tough place evaporated into the sweetest imaginable beaming, gentle smile as he listened to his daughter's voice. Salma's conversation has developed in leaps and bounds, and she had stories she wanted to tell him, and she wanted to sing him the ABC song - in fact, right there over the phones and behind the glass, singing to her baba, was the first time I've ever heard her complete the full alphabet. Then she laid on her back on the little metal counter, her head on the pillow of her sweater, and kicked her feet together to show him how the little lights flash and sparkle. He was smitten. Melted. Restored to peace. Soul healed, by her gentle innocence. This is what they 're depriving those fathers of. ** Brothers, husbands, sons. Friends, cousins, neighbors, coworkers. Teachers, employees, leaders, friends. Fathers. The cruelty is breathtaking, and the callousness beggars belief. Gratitude to everyone who fights this fight, who advocates, who goes and visits the ones who have no one, who keeps up the pressure. We need you. They need you. We can't do this without you. They can't do this alone. Now that Zahid's case is before the district court, structured as an emergency habeas petition, things are likely to move fast. The court will probably docket the case by tomorrow morning (Friday). The judge will probably issue some form of ruling within 24-48 hours. They might seek more information, or they might immediately order his release - the timeline is impossible to predict exactly, but I put it at 70% odds he'll be home with us sometime in the next two weeks. So I shift my attention to reintegration planning. Dim rooms, soft lights, healthy food, gentle touch, good work to do. Medical care. Reminders of home, familiar smells and flavors, time for whatever comes - bursts of chatter, hypervigilance, disrupted sleep, need for silence, emotional dysregulation, reduced mental processing capability... the combination of traumatic brain injury and chronic pain with months of unrelieved threat, overstimulation, sleep deprivation, nutritional insufficiency, and assaults on dignity, meaning, and hope - is not a gentle recipe. He is an unusual person, truly remarkable in his gentleness, patience, flexibility, and good humor - but he is human, and he has been through one version of hell. The fundraiser is still live - friends who would ask what you can do, that is one thing. Money stabilizes when all else is uncertain, and sustains the ability to be fully present and devote all my attention to co-regulation, to calm presence, to breathing and being beside him while he puts back together his soul. Meantime, friends, hug your families close please. Take a long walk on a beautiful autumn day and watch the leaves fall. Enjoy a good meal. Put down the phones. Do something kind for a neighbor; and do something to bring justice for someone more vulnerable than you. Remember that we weave the world together by our thoughts, our actions, our relationships. Remember that putting good out into the world is the purpose of our lives. In the Quran, it says, that after a period of hardship, Allah grants ease. I will be grateful for the rest of my life for the love and support you have given. Our family is blessed, and I am committed to using what we've been given to help others. The fight is not over. But we'll get through this - together. | | ---|---|--- You 're currently a free subscriber to "It's a Matter of Integrity" by Melissa Chaudhry. ## US Outlines Plan to End Ukraine War
The United States has developed a sweeping [28-point framework aimed at ending](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1u8zAMQE8jbwpMyn8ZNHyLt3xrR0O2qIStLBmSkjS3LxT0Bt0IPOCRfB-X5WLYc7j-Nzvp4uIS6Jk9lUJpuX8lw4EOb0Kg4jx_G2vzavKCLfYSQCIs1rB_LV1jtSNCUg1pGAc1ogIYmpseHTlwmzLnkVTfrWZyfW-3qbOw9SOphnW1ASAAtD2oUzsAqdZM69qhw-EsupYsl5hOn5FDuZHzr_igdNri3nh9K-XIQv0TOAucw-uIuVQkcK5igTPAexY437Os_wmcMwWOSd6zjM7xxsZnucXgOO3SUjHsK5E4yaMulTWCLFFSsPK3i3yaJHBukrbHk73nPIyia6-7Yf--rfwp6EPjTwAAAP__S4mJzw) the nearly four-year-old war between Russia and Ukraine, which reportedly includes provisions for territorial freezes, troop caps, and economic reintegration for Moscow. The plan, developed in part through consultations led by U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff with both Russian and Ukrainian officials, is the most detailed vision yet for ending the conflict, though it is viewed by some Ukrainian [officials as a potential "capitulation](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu4yAQBdCvsTssD3YgW1Bsky7bbmkNZkgmweAFHCd_v_LT-4PXzkhX99y_1-mKHDje_uBCpvo0RdpLoFopT9szI0daA8ZI1Qd-o3PFYplkL08CQEiYHHL4TGPrjCeSNLRkQKtBywFAtXcz6wHhjOdej8pLADt7qb1FZ7UardUtmyMNQAJAf4Kh6xXQ0OPZ2lF6qX41Y0-Oa8rdI3Gsd_Lhk16UuzktbTD3WtfSDL8beWnkZd_3zqf3oTj-xyXl4Bp52UQReSuFUbiMvoqVcCZx6MS3VGT6t3HmeBMLPlIWc4ozlcIpFuFzWsTzw682G7fuHAIXpZuxvy3I4atM_dGCLyP_BwAA__995Ihy)." Senior U.S. officials told reporters that they received "positive feedback" on the majority of the plan from Ukraine's Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council. Ukrainian President Volodymyr [Zelensky is expected to discuss](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L-O1DAQx_GncbpZxeP8uS1SLEKpOASioIwm8WR3WMeObN-Z8PQoiDe4-qsZ6ff5-Tq9kjjx96-08ZDXMHkuyXHOHKe3ZyTxvDvynvPq5DdZm2ZKE9bYgtaAerIk7piayg4rM7KpeNB9Z3o0WnfVYzBmbfvacNv3zdyQvSK-tMt6bTrLV66bSobzm9aota5bbS51p9nU9DLPDa7YXVVTs5Uc4uVXEJ8fvLojvHO8LGGr3PDIeU_K3BSOCsdSymVL_mwKR_ZwnxWOe3CSZUkKx_t56jf2WeH4hx379JQDEh0JHgySIDLZA3KAEuITgoe3BDMtT7ZwUpyFvYVCEcTDfySFI0W43fT3b1-oU2YMi1hlPn86bbmkHxz3Kg52L-KcpK5XTX3fSNy_FflD9O8D_g0AAP__n5CZbw) the plan with President Trump in the coming days, a meeting that will determine how Ukraine chooses to proceed with the sensitive proposals.
## Dick Cheney Eulogized at National Cathedral
Former Vice President Dick Cheney was memorialized at a funeral service held at Washington National Cathedral on Thursday, attended by more than 1,000 guests, including [former Presidents George W. Bush and Joe Biden](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OnjAQxJ8GOiPvmn9fQZGG7tKmRAbWsLnFRsZ8hHv6iEh5gutGmtFPM_PrY_iwLOyXn3ajLrkweLoOoZQoDudntOxpF-s9JSf8x87zMdpjQI2VAlAIw2xZ7qHM584RIZmcOmhq06ABqPO1AzTOlo2jstZWY1W3jaGxhZdrX7rSVc7dQwNAANAVmELXQEbbdhxLdFi_slLTzCnE4ndgn1Zycoc3xWIKWy7dmtJ-ZOZHhn2G_XVdxW3XEB43w_6Zk2G_B-HE0yOF35RhP_P0qaaVPN3KnZ6iFeVOETU9bLuQWijEhdSlxvNYlfDX_zidEhb-IuVC3Ciq966ghFbrxlTFmjbJYzfvF4vwUTdZqZfNsvyrm7718bvDvwEAAP__C-ORdQ) and all four living former vice presidents (Dan Quayle, Al Gore, Mike Pence, and Kamala Harris). Cheney, who died on Nov. 3 at age 84, was eulogized by Bush, who called him the "best choice for vice president," and by his daughter, former Congresswoman Liz Cheney, who described her father as "a giant to the end." The service acknowledged his extensive career, which included roles as Defense Secretary and White House Chief of Staff, but the event was also notable for the [absence of President Trump](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZD1yG9awAcElZHvphahxtwffGoNsz3Dz9yfmFzarUklPVfXna_6iEEO6_6ZNxur3OclZotQqeX58ZwpJjkgpSfUx_CPmslCZjTYfgAgGZ6YQX3PX8OhFjLSNjNjbtjctom3WcbB996kRB2cd904G651GOwyD7nvP0oTxoiEaRNQf2N60RWk1DcvSGW_sp-q0cKh7vv3dQ6qr-Pjan5Jvbt-aOK61HkW1v5SZlJnS69hLvSJlpguszIT41spMjwLXPmUmDu4b3CpJXuAfSTJF4ExngSXcgWWDRJtcjiXBSjmHAhsx7yeca4gCNT-2AygxPCk5gbtUWCS5VViZqckjH2eIMRTbq07fNwrx3bj-6ObnaP4HAAD__5TfkVI) and Vice President JD Vance, who were not invited following Cheney's public criticism of Trump.
## List: Most Popular Thanksgiving Sides
A new national survey confirms that for most Americans, the [sides are the real stars of the Thanksgiving table](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1yqzAQRp8GOjHaFX8uVNzGnW-bklmsFWwsBINkE94-40zeIP0335lzPm7DjSRInP7Twjb7dYh8pMA58z48HztJ5C1QjJx9kC9yLo2UBtTYKACFMDiScA516axnRjYlW-ha06EBaMvZuot3QL2p7x6db7wZsadO-7679C2ZrhT7fgNAANANmEq3wEZTP441emwvRa3ZSV736nOVmGf24VxfvFf3dSmDnXPeUmH-FXgt8HocR5Vk2cK58102Tu9VgddlTVlt6_YMtKs8U3ykSV4SJ5XEsXKSZjWeKmXKrH71-rrXdVPu1m2HhCCp7YpaTwtJ-GHnPwV7WfwOAAD__-qzf-A), with 63% of respondents preferring the trimmings over the turkey entrée. Stuffing or dressing remains the undisputed champion for the fourth straight year, claiming the top spot in 42 states. Mashed potatoes were also a strong favorite, topping the list in nine states, including Kansas and Washington. The cheesy favorite macaroni and cheese is rapidly gaining ground, securing the number one spot in states like Florida and New York, with Southern states such as Georgia and Mississippi showing a strong regional preference for creamy and sweet comfort foods. You can find out which [dish won in your state here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SozAQRk8DmSh182cCBZs486YbUg1qoNdCoiQZxref8lxh8q--V-_9e4wPEid-_Us7m7yE0fOVHOfMcXw9I4nnw5H3nBcnX2RtmiiNqLFVAAphtCTuPTalNQszcl2ygb6re6wBunIz2LWtnWieeoal0U0_6HaumwEH6Gle2lLM5w0AAUC3UFe6A6413aapwQW7oWg0W8khVv-D-Lzx4t7h5FjNYS-d2XI-UlH_KfBe4P26ruqjcDE_P4MC7zsdag8pqyMcL0dR5Y38M61yil9VEsvKStoUnxzfKmXKrEAPt5vu-jIae1zinKSuLxq97iTuB5x_Ves0-B0AAP__Iq9_Gg).

| Letter from the Chair
---
Will Nebraska Democrats Try Again to Impose Ranked-Choice Voting--and Permanently Tilt the Legislature Left?
Dear Nebraska Republicans,
Nebraska's officially non-partisan Unicameral is one of the reddest legislatures in America, yet Democrats have repeatedly punched above their weight. Expect Ranked-Choice Voting (RCV) to perennially resurface in the upcoming sessions, backed by the usual out-of-state dark money that fueled the 2024 abortion petitions. Why are national left-wing groups so obsessed with changing Nebraska's system? Because RCV would hand urban Democrats a structural jackpot in a state they otherwise cannot win statewide.
How would RCV rig the elections? In a red or purple district, Democrats could: Run an "independent" or No Labels-style candidate as the first choice for moderate Republicans and right-leaning independents.
Instruct their base to rank the actual Democrat second.
Watch the "independent" get eliminated and nearly all those votes flow straight to the Democrat--without moderates ever having to admit they voted D in the first round.
This is exactly how Lisa Murkowski won in Alaska and how Democrats flipped two "non-partisan" Virginia House seats in 2023 under RCV. It's fusion voting by another name, and it's a gold ticket for the minority party in a one-house legislature. Democrats already enjoy existing structural advantages in Nebraska. The Unicameral system itself is annually overwhelmed with an enormous number of bills and no second house to act as a firewall to slow the process that would allow for more public scrutiny. The low pay for legislators skews the talent pool heavily Democrat, especially in urban districts. Another structural advantage is hiding the "D" brand on non-partisan ballots and/or running effectively Democrat candidates as independents, moderates or even Republicans in some instances.
Add RCV on top of these three advantages and rural, conservative Nebraska effectively loses control of its own legislature--forever.
Nebraskans' default instinct to be polite and "give everyone a fair hearing" has already cost us in numerous instances including the structural advantages already mentioned. Being nice is a virtue--until it becomes unilateral disarmament. Nebraska Republicans need to treat any future RCV push as an existential threat and kill it early, hard, and without apology. The alternative is waking up in ten years to a permanently blue (or at least purple) Unicameral in the middle of the reddest heartland state in America.
That's not fearmongering. That's math.
Onward.
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

| What's Happening:
Candidate Recruitment....
I've had dozens of people ask me the same questions lately:
"What makes a good candidate?" "Am I actually qualified to run?" "Does my background even fit the job?"
Here's the truth: Most normal, hardworking conservatives are far more qualified than they realize. (Reminder: We currently have a Supreme Court justice who can't define what a woman is. The bar is not as high as you think.)
That said, if you want to win a competitive local Republican race today--county commissioner, state representative, state senate, sheriff, city council, school board, etc.--in a red or purple area, there are six non-negotiable qualities you must bring to the table:

* Time to Campaign: Local races are won (or lost) in the trenches. Plan on a minimum of 8 months of non-stop evenings and weekends knocking on doors, attending fish fries, parade-walking, and showing up at every chamber breakfast and Rotary lunch. The candidate with a 9-to-5 job or young kids at home may get outworked by the retired businessman, the stay-at-home mom with grown kids, or the self-employed guy who can set his own hours. Be ready to view your campaign as a full-time job.

* Good Communicator: Voters at the county fair or the church fellowship hall don't want 10-point plans--They want someone who can grab a mic (or no mic) at the county fair and explain in two plain, fired-up sentences why property taxes are crushing families--and exactly what you'll do about it.

* Money to Run or the Willingness to Ask for it Relentlessly: Even a State Legislative race in a rural district can cost $250,000+, and countywide or local races in growing suburbs routinely hit 4 figures. If you can't pick up the phone and call 300 people for $500 checks, or host living-room fundraisers every week, you'll be outspent on mail, radio, and digital ads.

* Pre-established Relationships in the Community: The first endorsements, the first volunteers, and the first big checks always go to the person that the farm bureau, the home-school leaders, the pastors, the volunteer fire department, and the big ranching families have known and trusted for 10-20 years--not the newcomer with slick flyers. Local activists and donors back people, not resumes.

* Foundational alignment with the Republican platform: This is the non-negotiable entry ticket. This is your entry ticket. At the Lincoln-Reagan dinner nobody quizzes you on guns, life, taxes, school choice, or parental rights--they already know because they've watched you fight those battles for years. You showed up to stop the tax increase, spoke against porn in school libraries, marched for life, and kept your Thin Blue Line flag flying. A spotless, long-term track record means no one wastes time wondering if you'll fold once elected.

* Genuinely Authentic and Approachable Personality: This is the multiplier. People will give up their Saturdays and put signs in their yards only for someone they genuinely like and trust--the candidate who remembers their name and their wife's cancer battle, asks about their grandkids' Little League game, and shows up in muddy boots looking like the neighbor who'd help change your tire--not some polished, distant figure who radiates Wall Street or country-club elitism. If you can't connect on a human level, if you come across as stiff, superior, or transactional, volunteers vanish and turnout drops. In low-turnout local primaries, that personal warmth and relatability isn't optional--it's the margin of victory.

Miss even one of these six, and you'll almost certainly finish second to the candidate who has them all.
If you're that person, or you know someone who is, and they'd like to talk it through, have them reach out to me anytime at political@ne.gop. I'm happy to grab coffee or jump on a call and walk through the next steps--no pressure, just honest conversation.

Nebraska's future isn't going to be saved in Washington -- it's going to be saved one county courthouse, one school board, and one legislative seat at a time. We don't need perfect people; we need principled fighters who are willing to show up, speak plain truth, and outwork everyone else. If that sounds like you -- or like your neighbor, your pastor, your kid's coach, or the farmer down the road -- then 2026 is your year. Reach out today, and let's get to work taking our state back. The bench is deeper than you think... and the clock is ticking.
In Liberty, Joe Hagerty Political Director Nebraska Republican Party political@ne.gop

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair Will Nebraska Democrats Try Again to Impose Ranked-Choice Voting--and Permanently Tilt the Legislature Left? Dear Nebraska Republicans, Nebraska's officially non-partisan Unicameral is one of the reddest legislatures in America, yet Democrats have repeatedly punched above their weight. Expect Ranked-Choice Voting (RCV) to perennially resurface in the upcoming sessions, backed by the usual out-of-state dark money that fueled the 2024 abortion petitions. Why are national left-wing groups so obsessed with changing Nebraska's system? Because RCV would hand urban Democrats a structural jackpot in a state they otherwise cannot win statewide. How would RCV rig the elections? In a red or purple district, Democrats could: Run an "independent" or No Labels-style candidate as the first choice for moderate Republicans and right-leaning independents. Instruct their base to rank the actual Democrat second. Watch the "independent" get eliminated and nearly all those votes flow straight to the Democrat--without moderates ever having to admit they voted D in the first round. This is exactly how Lisa Murkowski won in Alaska and how Democrats flipped two "non-partisan" Virginia House seats in 2023 under RCV. It's fusion voting by another name, and it's a gold ticket for the minority party in a one-house legislature. Democrats already enjoy existing structural advantages in Nebraska. The Unicameral system itself is annually overwhelmed with an enormous number of bills and no second house to act as a firewall to slow the process that would allow for more public scrutiny. The low pay for legislators skews the talent pool heavily Democrat, especially in urban districts. Another structural advantage is hiding the "D" brand on non-partisan ballots and/or running effectively Democrat candidates as independents, moderates or even Republicans in some instances. Add RCV on top of these three advantages and rural, conservative Nebraska effectively loses control of its own legislature--forever. Nebraskans' default instinct to be polite and "give everyone a fair hearing" has already cost us in numerous instances including the structural advantages already mentioned. Being nice is a virtue--until it becomes unilateral disarmament. Nebraska Republicans need to treat any future RCV push as an existential threat and kill it early, hard, and without apology. The alternative is waking up in ten years to a permanently blue (or at least purple) Unicameral in the middle of the reddest heartland state in America. That's not fearmongering. That's math. Onward. ## Uvalde County Judge Suspended
Uvalde County Judge William Mitchell was [suspended without pay](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2ynDAMx09jOu8gPwNLQZGG7qVNyQgsgxKvzdgCdm-fIVdIo-Knmf_Xr-_pGzlwXH_iiwZ5-zRFukogEcrTlnKhkwtLEcwryZwTuhnjZGrTaABtYHLI4TPZyg1z7XqoaICu_epM29TPahsaWKBpoeucXRbonXNk6bnY2TfQY0MVD7cYgAEwNdjmQb21c_v0NVLd9q1XtibHkvJDNhJ6Y_Hhk07KjyW9qjBsIntRXz-UGZUZr-t6_Cko91OZ8W6jzHgTzfGkIryi0M1uW2VGgPv0yozHicGRXtIR5aN_H24lXY6yU3Tk9MWypUP0jh-NXijrjYvm6HiRF0XRKerkPS-MQad9z1QKp6jMWOXB7ReHwKXtlK3XF3L4F17-b_JzMH8DAAD__5s1mMM) by the State Commission on Judicial Conduct on Tuesday after he was indicted for official oppression earlier this month. The [misdemeanor charge](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMHOnCAUhZ8Gd3cCjDLOgsVsXHWaNGnSpbnIRWkQJoD6-_aN_yt0fZLvnPP9eY9v9MHH-SeupOuXS2OkowSqlfK4pFxo98XXUjHPVE1OaA3GUXLZgRAgxWjRh3NsG6sNt0_RkBYPdX9I1fG-WfREtr07wzvuDJmnUkZgj1NvjJv6rueN1xdMCCmE5KLtbvRsW6N6x5G4eirHWk7W15RvdaFKX1hcONNO-TaltQl6qfVT2P3F5MDkcBzHbS3xypgcKMJWmByuU0wOU_YrMTl8U2BKW6wn_N3sTFC28qFoyQK6ShkwBJrJhhO2GPBwWwgnWKroo48zbJ8CNvudMhxLAowzZbKw-KsVM7xe4teP_fe7ydp-Dh-CL-rBWj6v6MP38Pp_unct_wUAAP__JECZEg) stems from a March incident in which Mitchell ordered the arrest of a UPS driver, Tyler Cox, who left packages for the third floor of the county courthouse on the first floor because the elevator was broken. Mitchell allegedly yelled at Cox, grabbed his loaded dolly, and seized his cell phone. Cox claims he was detained for five minutes without being read his Miranda rights. Cox, 29, [filed a $15 million lawsuit](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdEa2Q-xQuNiGLttuiQY8hpEMjuwJhL9f5f3C66_u0Tn_nuMTKNG-_IUNPX9iHnc8a0JmLOOaS8WDKnFlKAvyVDKECfbRKHOXWkujxwCUrrFrgp9U6HWDXjt7c8be1aNZvZuMA-sCaO2MispGN9np0Xeqd7fYq4b890xro7VRuru32HfdZB9RASrb2yg6hYE4l5ZXZPxAjenKB5Z2zluT_Mr8quL2R5hBmOE8z_Z9QAqYEAKWr853KMwAhWlOWIUZ5vyRW2bKe5WcZcEtHyjn_N75qjLBeWGRsdCChbIwQ1N8eJ2UElXrRKeWDSj98Pl31Q5v_gcAAP__VJSEAA) against Mitchell and the county, and he recently requested a change of venue. **Have you or a loved one experienced the overcrowded chaotic world of a Hospital Emergency Department (ED)?**

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecd96955-88e3-4f01-bb5d-ca2bed207101?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

[Source](https://substack.com/redirect/210d7de6-ee6d-4f29-8efa-193a57f8ca91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
An ED is supposed to be where acutely ill or those suffering from life threatening conditions go. **It is also where those who cannot see their doctors go for routine care**.
**Lack of basic appointments, coupled with the use of EDs for primary care for those on Medicaid (who sometimes call 9-1-1 to chauffeur them to a doctor), coupled with excessive illegal immigration who use EDs as their Primary Care Physician** has led to an overcrowded, overwhelmed ED especially in poorer communities and especially in the winter.
When it has been determined that you or a loved one is sick enough to be hospitalized what should happen is that you are admitted and taken to your hospital room.
Unfortunately, that is not often the case. Instead, you are left in the ED, not receiving the care as a seriously ill person requires while they wait for a hospital bed. This waiting in the emergency department for a bed is called **BOARDING**.
In a recent article in Medscape Medical News (dated November 11, 2025) entitled "_**When The Waiting Never Ends. How Emergency Department Boarding Hits Hospitalists And How To Solve It**_ " sheds light on this problem. Most of you have probably never heard of the term boarding, but this is what happens and what it is called in EDs throughout the country.
In January of 2022, 40% of the patients that were admitted to the hospital in the ED had to wait more than four hours in the ED before they could have a hospital bed, and 6% stayed longer than 24 hours. These are the sick patients that need emergency hospitalization, and the longer they sit in the ED before they are admitted to the hospital for proper care the sicker they get.
**Also, by being in a general population as a susceptible patient, these Boarders are also exposed to the plethora of contagious infectious diseases of all the coughing and breathing ED patients sitting in the waiting rooms while they wait**.
**The Northeast Conundrum - Increased Boarding in Winter Months**
Boarding is exacerbated in the Northeast during the winter time where up to 8% of the patients spend 24 hours in the ED waiting for a bed. _**Imagine a seriously ill patient spending 24 hours in the ED, not receiving the level of care they need and probably not being fed on a regular basis. Also,**_ **imagine the strain on the family member who is waiting there.**
The article went on to conclude that long boarding times and holding in the ED results in higher mortality, longer lengths of stay, and greater readmission risks. _**Certainly none of these results in Making America Healthier Again.**_
**WHAT IS THE SOLUTION? - Proactive Care and Avoidance of the ED**
If you have an acute illness that is not life threatening, the best place for you to be seen is by you own doctor. Unfortunately, our healthcare system has consolidated into an institution and a hospital-based healthcare system that no longer accommodates these urgent visits. _**Take a look at every physician practice, there is a big Hospital emblem or logo or affiliation.**_
To make an appointment, you either go online or call a call center where a non-medical scheduler fits you into available slots in a doctor's schedule based on availability. If there is no availability then you cannot be seen.
**What about the Urgent Care Centers? Can they alleviate the Strain on the ED?**
If you cannot see your Primary Care Physician, your next option is the Urgent Care Center (most are owned and operated by the hospitals). These facilities can handle common illnesses, but if you need specialty care or have an uncommon illness they are not the right fit. They are good for your basic workup and despite often being Board Certified, they are reduced to an elevated LPN.
_Once you have experienced an Urgent Care Center, most (except hypochondriacs) get frustrated by the lack of immediate solutions to their illnesses that they do not come back._
**So If Urgent Care isn 't an option - Where do you Go? - Take a Seat in the ED**
If you cannot see your physician and Urgent Care is out of the question, you are back at the ED. If your symptoms do not warrant a triage approach, take a number, fill out a form and take a seat. _Also expect to pick up a new disease you didn 't have before in the cesspool of contractible illnesses. Maybe you will pick up some new rare and foreign infection._ **So now the ED is a double edged sword.**
_**If you 're really sick then you could be waiting a long time for a bed while you get sicker.**_
So How do we solve this? We cannot treat your life like a seat on an airplane.
**Airlines tend to oversell seats as they know there are cancellations. Thus they overbook - THIS SHOULD NOT BE THE BUSINESS MODEL FOR MEDICINE**
Institutions that provide outpatient care **MUST** leave slots open in their schedules to fit in urgent patients.
**The Real Solution:**
**WE MUST RESTORE PRIVATE PRACTICES WITHOUT THE HOSPITAL RUN POLICIES AND PROCEDURES SO THAT THEY CAN REVERT BACK TO ACCOMODATING SICK PATIENTS WITH THESE "EMERGENCIES" SO THEY NO LONGER FLOOD THE ED**.
_**Other Boarding Issues - Hospital After Care**_
Coordination of care between the ED and the Hospital to determine how hospitalized patients awaiting discharge can be discharged more efficiently and when necessary be transferred to other facilities must be resolved, especially where the patient needs a discharge to a rehab or nursing home type facility. The inability to find a bed after discharge causes boarding issues on the front end.

_**Teamwork and identifying problems is the first step to a solution.**_
In the past I served on the Operating Room Committee of my hospital. Our concern was that operating rooms were running late, causing problems for patients, doctors and creating staffing issues.
Our Committee included, Surgeons, Anesthesia, O.R. Nursing Supervisors, Admitting Supervisors and Nursing Supervisors and other Hospital Administrators. We would get reports every month on the number and percentage of cases that were delayed and **why** they were delayed. _**The result of this collaboration was a reduction in delays and a more efficiently running operating room.**_
_**The same collaborative team effort, which has been done in some hospitals needs to be expanded. Hospitals should have to report their boarding times and when they are too high hospital reimbursements should be reduced. Also, it can potentially result in shifting Ambulance routes to alternate hospitals and EDs (especially in larger cities).**_
_**Finance Drives Healthcare**_
By incentivizing/penalizing Hospitals, it will create the financial incentive to force hospitals to admit sick patients faster, shorten hospital stays, reduce unnecessary deaths and free up overwhelmed EDs to take care of their sick patients.
**By Addressing these issues - We actually can Make America Healthier Again**

subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- November 21
body:

Dear friends and neighbors, As we head into the holiday season, I would like to wish everyone a Happy Thanksgiving! I hope that you have the opportunity to spend time with family, friends, and those you love. I am also happy to share that we just launched our brand new website! It's a one-stop-shop for all of your needs. Whether you need assistance with your Social Security, have an immigration question, are looking to book a Capitol tour, or apply for an internship in our office - you can head to our new website to get it done! You can learn more about my committee assignments, legislation I have sponsored and cosponsored, my voting record, or sign up to follow us on social media. I encourage you to head to [www.alsobrooks.senate.gov](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15679.14674029.5767892.7190525&report_id=&redirect=http%3a%2f%2fwww.alsobrooks.senate.gov&redir_log=60291809476229) to check it out. \----------- As you know, the recent Republican government shutdown - the longest shutdown in U.S. history - ended last week. I voted NO on the Continuing Resolution because after weeks of refusing to negotiate, Senate Republicans put forward a CR that reaffirmed their indifference to the heath care crisis and affordability crisis in our nation. I made a promise to the people of Maryland that I would always vote in their best interests, and that's why I voted no. The first 11 months of this Administration have been a disaster. From soaring energy costs to soaring grocery prices to catastrophic tariffs, the lives of everyday hardworking Americans have gotten more difficult, not better. This Administration has made our families sicker, and Republicans have yet to fix the health care crisis that's unfolding as we speak. It's time they step up and extend the ACA tax credits to prevent millions from losing coverage, and premiums from spiking for those who can least afford it. Your voice matters in this. For me, it's the only voice that matters. And that's why I'll continue to fight back. **Fighting Through Legislation** I continue fighting for Marylanders on the floor of the Senate, and I wanted to share just some of the legislation I have led or cosponsored over the last few weeks, including legislation that seeks to minimize the negative impacts on families and federal workers in the event of future lapses in appropriations.
Healthy Maternal and Obstetric Medicine (MOM) Act
* This bill would ensure that all women eligible for coverage through the Affordable Care Act (ACA) insurance marketplaces, as well as women eligible for other individual or group health plan coverage, can access affordable health care coverage throughout their pregnancies. The bill would establish a special enrollment period (SEP) for expectant mothers. Currently, marriage, divorce, having a baby, adoption, and changing jobs are considered qualifying life events that trigger a special enrollment period; however, becoming pregnant is not considered a qualifying event. The Healthy MOM Act would change that.

Federal Worker Mortgage Forbearance Act
* This bill would require 90 days of mortgage forbearance for federal workers and contractors with federally-backed mortgage loans.

Shutdown Student Loans for Feds Act
* This bill would require the Department of Education to pause student loan payments for federal workers - including federal contractors and military personnel - in the event of a federal government shutdown lasting longer than two weeks.

HELP Feds Act
* Ensures federal employees who are required to work during a government shutdown are eligible to apply for unemployment insurance.

Boosting Benefits and COLAs for Seniors Act
* This legislation would direct the Social Security Administration to adjust benefits based on the Consumer Price Index for Americans aged 62 or older (CPI-E) rather than the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners (CPI-W), if CPI-E would result in a larger increase in benefits, and; direct the Bureau of Labor Statistics to calculate and publish the CPI-E on a monthly basis.

Voter Purge Protection Act
* This legislation would prohibit the removal of individuals from official state voter rolls due to changes in residence or not voting in previous elections, stipulate that only verifiable and objective evidence (such as a death or permanent move to other state) can result in removal from voter rolls, and require notification to registered voters about their removal and how to contest.

Background Check Expansion Act
* This legislation would expand federal background checks to nearly all gun sales.

Right to Representation for VA Workers Act
* This bill would codify VA employees' Weingarten right to be represented by a person of an employee's choosing during an investigation that may result in disciplinary action against the employee. The Weingarten right is a long-held principle protected through collective bargaining agreements.

Anti-Cash Grab Act
* This legislation would repeal a provision--quietly added into the Senate government funding bill by U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) at the last minute--that allows senators to collect $500,000 for every phone record lawfully obtained.

True Shutdown Fairness Act
* This legislation would have ensured pay for all federal workers, federal contractors, and our military during the government shutdown.

Keep Head Start Funded Act
* This legislation would provide funding for Head Start programs during a government shutdown and prevent disruptions for children and families in need.

Securing Assurance for Federal Employees Act
* This legislation would prohibit any federal agency from carrying out a reduction in force (RIF) during a lapse in appropriations, ensuring that federal employees cannot be permanently laid off during a government shutdown.

Keep SNAP and WIC Funded Act of 2025
* This bill provides FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to continue operating the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP); the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC); and a related block grant program if there is a lapse in FY2026 appropriations for USDA.

Emergency Relief for Federal Contractors Act
* This legislation would allow penalty-free distributions from retirement accounts in the case of certain federal contractors impacted by federal government shutdowns.

Fair Pay for Federal Contractors Act
* This legislation would provide automatic backpay for federal contractors during a government shutdown.

Restoring Access to Detainees Act
* This legislation would ensure that families can contact each other and lawyers have access to their clients when they come into ICE custody and when they are transferred between facilities. The bill would also codify portions of the current detention standards concerning detainee access to communications with oversight entities and would codify the free phone minutes program, ensuring that noncitizens can make outgoing calls.

No Nuclear Testing Act
* This legislation would prohibit the use of federal funds for any explosive nuclear weapons test, while preserving stockpile stewardship activities consistent with the zero-yield standard. The bill reaffirms America's commitment to responsible nuclear policy and global arms control.

Social Security Emergency Inflation Relief Act
* This legislation would provide economic recovery payments to recipients of social security, supplemental security income, railroad retirement benefits, and veterans disability compensation or pension benefits.

No Argentina Bailout Act
* This legislation would stop the $40 billion bailout the Trump Administration is providing for Argentina.

National Native American Heritage Act Resolution
* This bipartisan resolution recognizes National Native American Heritage Month and celebrates the heritages and cultures of Native Americans and the contributions of Native Americans to the United States.

American-Speech-Language-Hearing Association Resolution
* This resolution commemorates the centennial year of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association.

SNAP During the Shutdown Resolution
* This resolution expresses the sense of the Senate that the Trump Administration is legally obligated to fund the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) through the use of the contingency fund (during the government shutdown).

National Wildlife Refuge Week Resolution
* This bipartisan resolution designated the week beginning on October 12, 2025 as "National Wildlife Refuge Week."

Navy 250th Birthday Resolution
* This bipartisan resolution recognized the 250th birthday of the United States Navy.

Book Banning Resolution
* This resolution expresses concern about the growing problem of book banning, and the proliferation of threats to freedom of expression in the United States.

**In the Community** It was such a joy to meet with Maryland high schoolers who came to visit me on Capitol Hill this week. These students came from all across our great state to discuss critical legislation and how I can best represent them. I reminded them they are our future. Their voices matter. It was a joy to join State Senator Nick Charles, Special Secretary Yolanda Maria Martinez, and the Prince George's Chamber of Commerce for a Fireside Chat to discuss how I'm fighting for our small businesses. It was great to have the opportunity to hear from Howard County residents alongside my colleagues Rep. Sarah Elfreth, Attorney General Anthony Brown, and Comptroller Brooke Lierman. Marylanders are sick of this Administration's cruelty and clear inability to govern. We will continue to fight back and stand strong for Maryland values. It was great to meet with Charles County leadership to hear more on their priorities on how they plan to continue moving the county forward. I was proud to partner with local leaders and direct federal funding for SMRT and their CSM aviation program. I was honored to join Pastor John K. Jenkins and other faith leaders for the Master Series of Distinguished Clergy at First Baptist Church of Glenarden. Together, we will continue the fight for a just future -- a future where we can all live safely, with dignity, and thrive.
**Stay in the Fight ** I know these are difficult times. But please know that I will continue fighting for you every step of the way. We will not give up. We will not give in to this Administration, and I ask that you continue to fight alongside us. Please continue to reach out to us. You can call the office or connect with us at [alsobrooks.senate.gov](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15679.14674029.5767892.7190525&report_id=&redirect=http%3a%2f%2falsobrooks.senate.gov%2f&redir_log=346519414955204). You can also follow us on Bluesky, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, and X. We are in this TOGETHER. Sincerely, Angela D. Alsobrooks
United States Senator
